summary: Andy Hunter previews the 243rd Merseyside derby, with Liverpool strong at home but still seeking consistency under Jürgen Klopp after a midfield rebuild. Everton under Sean Dyche are improving, but have scored more than once in a league game only eight times in 12 months. Klopp stresses step-by-step progress, defensive organisation and the disruption caused by international breaks.
one_line: Ahead of the 243rd Merseyside derby, Klopp wants more consistency from a rebuilt Liverpool while Dyche's improving Everton threaten, despite poor goalscoring.
key_facts: Liverpool are three points off the top, have scored three goals in every Premier League home game and have a 100% record in all competitions at Anfield.
The Merseyside derby is the 243rd edition of the most played derby in English football.
Jürgen Klopp has lost one of his 17 encounters with Everton; Liverpool have lost one of the past 23 Premier League meetings at Anfield and one of the past 25 league derbies home or away.
Andy Robertson is out for up to three months with a shoulder injury, heightening Liverpool's defensive concerns.
Everton beat Bournemouth 3-0 last time out, only the eighth time in 12 months they have scored more than once in a Premier League match.
Everton have won three of their past four games under Sean Dyche.
Klopp said Everton are in a good moment and compared them to Dyche's Burnley: second-ball fights, runs in behind and a compact defence.
Liverpool beat Aston Villa 3-0 early last month in a performance echoing their dominant best under Klopp, but other displays have had lapses.
Klopp attributes some instability to the summer midfield rebuild and two international breaks interrupting preparations.
Mohamed Salah has scored or assisted in 14 consecutive Premier League matches.
Liverpool could match the 1980-81 side by scoring three or more goals in the opening four home league games.
Liverpool drew 2-2 at Brighton before the break, and Klopp had only three first-team players, plus a goalkeeper, in training until Wednesday.
Klopp says he likes to build teams from the defensive side but cannot do so in the middle of a season, calling his squad talented and creative but needing to 'organise protection'.
